portal_hypertension.abstract: Adipose tissue alterations are linked to adverse outcomes in patients with cirrhosis, but their role in portal vein thrombosis (PVT) is unclear. We aimed to evaluate the association between body composition and PVT. Cross-sectional study including patients with cirrhosis. Body adiposity was assessed by computed tomography (CT) at the third lumbar vertebra including visceral (VATI), subcutaneous (SATI) and total adipose (TATI) tissue indexes, bioimpedance analysis (BIA) including visceral fat area (VFA), total body fat (TBF) and total body fat percentage (TBF%), and anthropometry. portal_hypertension.abstract: Clinical trials in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) typically include patients with preserved liver function (Child-Pugh A), without adequately considering cirrhosis or clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH). We aimed to compare prognostic models in Child-Pugh A patients. This prospective multicenter cohort study included patients with advanced HCC treated with systemic therapy (2018-2024) in Latin America. Survival was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional multivariate hazards models and competing risk analysis for cause-specific mortality and hepatic decompensation. portal_hypertension.abstract: Azathioprine is widely used to treat inflammatory bowel disease, organ transplantation, and autoimmune disorders. Hepatotoxicity is a rare but serious complication. We report a 48-year-old man with ileocolonic Crohn's disease who developed azathioprine-induced portosinusoidal vascular disease (PSVD) after 15 years of treatment. Diagnosis was suspected due to persistent cytopenia (leukopenia and thrombocytopenia) and when transabdominal ultrasonography and upper gastrointestinal endoscopy showed signs of portal hypertension. portal_hypertension.abstract: Acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding (AUGIB) is a frequent life-threatening scenario in everyday clinical practice. We undertook a study to assess the etiology and important clinical outcomes in patients with significant AUGIB unstable for transfer to an endoscopy suite. This is a prospective observational study conducted between December 2019 and December 2022, including patients above the age of 16 years with a history of clinically significant AUGIB undergoing bedside endoscopy in an intensive care (ICU)/high dependency unit (HDU) setting. portal_hypertension.abstract: Compensated advanced chronic liver disease (cACLD) encompasses patients with advanced fibrosis/cirrhosis at risk for liver-related complications. The natural history of cACLD has been extrapolated from compensated cirrhosis and historic cohorts, although major advances in diagnosis and management have impacted the clinical course and understanding of disease trajectories. From 2015 to 2022, 1140 consecutive patients with cACLD (first-time liver stiffness measurement [LSM] ≥10 kPa) at the Vienna General Hospital were followed for first and further decompensation, and death.
